items.prompt: Black to move. Find the discovered check that wins the queen.

claims.statement: ...Ra3+ followed by ...Rxa7 wins the queen.
...Ra3+ is the engine's first choice.
Right now the king is not in check: the rook on f3 blocks the bishop.

hints: Which of your pieces is blocking another of your pieces' line?
The bishop on c6 aims at the white king, and your rook stands in the way.
Move the rook with a threat of its own: it can attack the queen on a7.
items.explain: The rook on f3 blocks the bishop's diagonal to the king. ...Ra3+ moves it away: the bishop gives check, and the rook now attacks the queen on a7. White must answer the check, so the rook takes the queen.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the discovered attack.

claims.statement: Bxh7+ followed by Rxe8 wins the queen for a bishop and a pawn.
Bxh7+ is the engine's first choice.
Right now the bishop on e4 stands between the rook and the queen.

hints: Your bishop stands in front of your rook on the e-file. What happens if it moves?
If the bishop moves without a threat, Black takes the rook first. The bishop's move must be forcing.
Which capture also gives check?
items.explain: Moving the bishop uncovers the rook's attack on the queen. Bxh7+ is also check, so Black has no time to take the rook. The king recaptures or steps aside, and the rook takes the queen.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's king stands on h8 instead of g8. Does Bxh7 still win the queen? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxh7 allows ...Qxe1 and White loses the rook.
Right now the bishop on e4 stands between the queen and the rook; once it leaves, the queen attacks e1.
The bishop attacks h7, but a bishop on h7 does not give check to a king on h8.

hints: After the bishop moves, who attacks the rook, and who attacks the queen?
It is Black's turn after Bxh7. Is Black in check?
items.explain: Both rook and queen attack each other once the bishop moves, but it is Black's turn. Bxh7 is not a check, so Black takes the rook on e1 first. A discovered attack works only if the moving piece makes a threat Black must answer.

items.prompt: White to move. The white rook stands on d1, not e1. Does Bxh7+ win the queen? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxh7+ Kxh7 loses the bishop for a pawn.
Nothing white aims at the queen on e8.

hints: Which white piece would attack the queen if the bishop moved?
items.explain: Nothing stands behind the bishop on the e-file, so moving it uncovers nothing. Bxh7+ Kxh7 just loses a bishop for a pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the move that gives double check.

claims.statement: ...Nxf5+ followed by ...Nxg7 wins a rook and a pawn for a pawn along the engine line.
...Nxf5+ is the engine's first choice.
Right now the white king is not in check: the knight on e3 blocks the rook.

hints: Your rook on c3 and the white king on g3 stand on the same rank. What is in between?
Move the blocker with a check of its own.
A knight on f5 attacks g3.
items.explain: The knight on e3 blocks the rook on c3 from the king on g3. ...Nxf5+ gives check with the knight and uncovers the rook's check at the same time. Only the king can answer a double check, and the knight then takes the rook on g7.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic? If so, play it.

claims.statement: ...f4+ followed by ...Rxh5 wins the rook for a pawn along the engine line.
...f4+ is the engine's first choice.

hints: Does any of your pieces block another of your pieces?
The pawn on f5 stands between your rook and an enemy rook.
Move the pawn with check.
items.explain: The pawn on f5 blocks the rook on c5 from the rook on h5. ...f4+ gives check, and after the king deals with it the rook takes on h5.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic that wins material?

claims.statement: ...Bxh2 is not check, so White takes the rook on e8 and Black loses material.
The engine does not see a decisive advantage for either side.

hints: Which of your pieces blocks another of your pieces?
If you move the blocker, does the move make a threat the opponent must answer?
items.explain: The rook is behind the bishop, but the bishop's capture is no check, so the opponent simply takes the exposed rook first.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the back-rank mate.

claims.statement: Re8 is checkmate.
Re8# is the engine's first choice.
No black piece covers e8.

hints: The black king stands on the back rank behind its own pawns.
A rook check along the back rank needs an open file to reach it.
Look at e8.
items.explain: Re8 checks along the back rank. The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 take away the king's escape squares, nothing can capture the rook on e8, and nothing can block on f8. That is checkmate.

items.prompt: Black to move. What does White threaten? Move a White piece to show it.

claims.statement: If Black passes, Re8 is checkmate.
No black piece covers e8.

hints: Your king has no escape squares. Which line leads to your back rank?
A rook on the open e-file reaches e8.
items.explain: The white rook has the open e-file. Re8 would be mate: the king is shut in by its own pawns and nothing covers e8. Your own back rank is the weakness.

items.prompt: Black to move. White threatens Re8 mate. Give the king an escape square with one pawn move.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is among these three pawn moves, and all three are close in value.
...g6 also gives luft but is clearly lower in the engine's ranking.
...g5 loses a pawn to Bxg5, so it is clearly worse.
Without a defence, Re8 is mate.

hints: Which pawns stand in front of your king?
Move one of them so that the king can step off the back rank.
h6 gives the king the square h7.
items.explain: Moving a pawn in front of the king gives it luft, an escape square. After ...h6 a rook check on e8 is only a check, because the king can go to h7.

feedback_by_move.g7g5: This gives luft but drops a pawn: the bishop on c1 takes on g5.
feedback_by_move.g7g6: This also gives the king a square, but the engine rates it clearly lower than ...h6, ...h5 or ...f6.

items.prompt: White has just played Re8+. Black's h-pawn stands on h6. Is this checkmate?

claims.statement: Black is in check.
The king can step to h7.
Nothing black can capture the rook on e8, but the king has an escape square.

hints: List the squares next to the king. Which are free?
Which of them is attacked by the rook?
items.explain: The rook attacks the whole back rank, but h7 is empty and not attacked. The king steps there and the check is over. One pawn move turned a mating threat into a mere check.

items.prompt: White to move. A black bishop stands on d7. Is Re8+ still a winning back-rank mate? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Re8+ Bxe8 loses the rook.
The bishop on d7 covers e8.

hints: Who can capture a rook that lands on e8?
items.explain: The bishop on d7 covers e8, so the rook is simply taken. A back-rank mate needs a king with no escape square and nothing that can capture or block.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a mate in one?

claims.statement: ...Re1+ is met by a capture and loses the rook.
A white bishop covers e1.

hints: Which squares on White's back rank does the rook reach?
Can White capture a piece that lands on e1?
items.explain: The rook can check along the back rank, but a white bishop covers e1 and takes it. A check on the back rank is not mate if something can capture the checking piece.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a mate in one? If so, play it.

claims.statement: ...Re1 is checkmate.
...Re1# is the engine's first choice.

hints: Look at the white king and the squares next to it.
Which line leads to White's back rank?
The e-file is open.
items.explain: The white king is shut in by its own pawns, and nothing covers e1. ...Re1 is mate.

items.prompt: Black to move. Anything to worry about? Show the threat by moving a White piece, or say there is none.

claims.statement: If Black makes an unrelated move, Black does not lose more than a pawn along the engine line.
No white piece attacks h7, so the king can step there after a check.

hints: Does Re8 mate?
Count the king's escape squares.
items.explain: The h-pawn on h6 gives the king h7, so Re8+ is only a check. There is no mating threat.

items.prompt: Black to move. Win material by removing a defender.

claims.statement: ...Rxe2 followed by ...Qxg3+ wins material along the engine line.
...Rxe2 is the engine's first choice.
One white piece, the knight on e2, defends the rook on g3.

hints: Which white piece is attacked by the queen, and what defends it?
The rook on g3 has only one defender. Which?
Capture the knight on e2; after the recapture the queen takes on g3 with check.
items.explain: The rook on g3 is defended only by the knight on e2. ...Rxe2 removes the knight; after Rxe2 the queen takes the rook on g3 with check, and nothing recaptures.

items.prompt: Black to move. Win material by driving a defender away.

claims.statement: ...Qd4+ followed by ...Qxa1+ wins material along the engine line.
...Qd4+ is the engine's first choice.
One white piece, the rook on e1, defends the rook on a1.

hints: Which white piece defends the rook on a1?
Give a check that the defender is forced to answer.
The queen checks on d4.
items.explain: The rook on e1 defends the rook on a1. ...Qd4+ is check, and if the rook on e1 steps in front of the king it stops guarding a1, so the queen takes the rook with check.

items.prompt: Black to move. Win material by luring a piece to a bad square.

claims.statement: ...Rh1+ followed by ...Qxf1+ wins material along the engine line.
...Rh1+ is the engine's first choice.
One white piece, the king on g1, defends the queen on f1.

hints: The queen on f1 is defended by the king. Can the king be made to leave?
Offer the rook with check.
A rook on h1 gives check and the king is the only piece that can take it.
items.explain: The white queen on f1 is defended only by the king on g1. ...Rh1+ forces the king to take on h1, which leaves f1 undefended, and the black queen takes the white queen with check.

items.prompt: Black to move. One white piece defends two others. Win material by exploiting it.

claims.statement: ...Rxa2 wins material along the engine line.
...Rxa2 is the engine's first choice.
One white piece, the queen, defends the rook on a2.
The same queen is the only defender of the bishop on g5.

hints: Which white piece defends both the rook on a2 and the bishop on g5?
Attack one of the two so that the defender must choose.
Take the rook on a2.
items.explain: The white queen is the only defender of two pieces. If it recaptures on a2 it stops defending the bishop; if it stays, the rook is lost. A defender with two jobs cannot do both.

items.prompt: Black to move. A white pawn on f2 now also defends g3. Does ...Rxe2 still win material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: ...Rxe2 Rxe2 followed by ...Qxg3+ fxg3 loses material.
Two white pieces defend the rook on g3: the knight and the pawn.

hints: Count the defenders of g3 again.
After the knight is gone, what recaptures on g3?
items.explain: Removing the knight no longer works: the pawn on f2 also defends the rook, so ...Qxg3+ fxg3 loses the queen for a rook. The idea needs the removed piece to be the only defender.

items.prompt: Black to move. ...Re2+ wins material. Which idea is it?

claims.statement: ...Re2+ followed by ...Qxe4+ wins material along the engine line.
...Re2+ is the engine's first choice.
Only the king on e3 defends the queen on e4.

hints: The rook is offered for nothing. What does the capture force?
After the king captures, which square has it left?
items.explain: The rook is given up so that the king must capture it. The king leaves e3, and with it goes the defence of the queen on e4. Luring a piece to a bad square is a decoy.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a tactic? If so, play it.

claims.statement: Rxf5 followed by Rxh5+ wins material along the engine line.
Rxf5 is the engine's first choice.

hints: Which black pieces defend each other?
Take a defender, even if it is recaptured.
What does the rook on f5 defend?
items.explain: The rook on f5 defends the pawn on h5 along the fifth rank. Taking it, even at the price of a recapture, leaves the pawn undefended, and the other rook takes it with check.

items.prompt: Black to move. Does the rook sacrifice ...Re2+ win material?

claims.statement: ...Re2+ Rxe2 loses the rook along the engine line.
The king on e3 and the rook on d2 both cover e2.

hints: Who can capture a rook on e2?
A decoy needs the capturing piece to be forced to move away from its post.
items.explain: The rook on d2 can capture on e2, so the king does not have to move away. The lure fails and Black simply loses the rook.
